correctness.rationale: The definition, unit-sphere normalization, Birkhoff quantifier and asymmetric objective are reconstructed explicitly. Dihedral symmetry reduces x to an edge interior or one vertex. On an edge interior the unique norming functional forces y=(0,±1), giving two exact quadratic/linear branches. At a vertex, the norming-functional segment makes Birkhoff orthogonality equivalent to y_1(y_1+y_2)≤0, which cuts the unit octagon into exactly four line segments. The objective is evaluated on all four segments; two concave branches attain the common value (12+11√2)/8 and all other branches are strictly smaller. The displayed unit pair attains equality. The packaged symbolic checker independently verifies every branch maximum used after the support reduction.
risks: The verifier checks the algebraic branch optimization; the completeness of the case split rests on the explicit support-functional geometry of the octagon in RESULT.md.

value.rationale: The defining paper introduces T_perpendicular to quantify the interaction of the T-type geometric mean with Birkhoff orthogonality, derives only universal bounds and two endpoint-style examples, and explicitly identifies exact values on further specific spaces as an open computational direction. The regular octagon is a canonical non-Hilbert polyhedral plane used throughout Banach-space geometry. Its exact value is neither the Hilbert value nor the square endpoint, and the maximizer lies in the interior of an admissible support arc rather than at a pair of octagon vertices. This makes the computation a natural benchmark for how nonsmooth support geometry changes the invariant, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
risks: The contribution is a canonical exact benchmark rather than a classification theorem for polygonal norms.
